references.text: Earlier warning against making a covenant with the inhabitants of the land and their gods, which would become a snare for the Israelites
Moses repeats the prohibition against making a covenant with the peoples of Canaan
Warning that foreign gods will become a snare for Israel
Joshua warns against making a covenant with the remaining peoples, who will become a snare and trap for Israel
The angel of the Lord rebukes Israel for having made a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, which became a snare to them
Describes how Israel mixed with the nations and their deeds became a snare to them
Paul urges believers not to be yoked together with unbelievers, a parallel to the warning against making covenants with the nations
A direct thematic and linguistic parallel that confirms the warning that the inhabitants will become a snare leading to idolatry.
Expands on the warning by describing the concrete sufferings ('thorns and thistles') that arise when one ignores the 'snare' mentioned in Exodus.
Theological parallel between the physical 'snare' in the Old Testament and the spiritual deception in the New Testament, both leading people away from God.
